# Orzhov Removal Midrange

- **Format:** Casual 60-card, 1v1
- **Archetype:** Orzhov (W/B) removal midrange: kill nearly everything the opponent plays, draw extra cards, then win with big flyers, Grave Titan and planeswalkers
- **Played by:** either. It suits whoever enjoys a patient, reactive game, and it's a good deck to take on a stronger opponent
- **Status:** idea
- **Complexity:** 3/5
- **Estimated power:** 6.5 with owned cards only, 7.5 with the buys (on a 1v1 scale)
- **Configuration:** **Standalone strongest deck** (for games against stronger opponents). It borrows from other decks, as listed under Shared-pool conflicts.

Orzhov (white-black) removal midrange uses the two best removal colours in the collection. It carries about 15 ways to kill a creature, from 1-mana Swords to Plowshares to Hero's Downfall, plus extra card draw. Once the opponent runs out of threats, Lyra Dawnbringer, Desecration Demon, Grave Titan and (after upgrades) three planeswalkers take over. It's the strongest, most 'grown-up' deck, built to give an experienced player a proper game. It suits a player who likes answering threats and winning a long game more than racing.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **3x Murderous Rider // Swift End** (replaces Withering Torment, Ayli, Eternal Pilgrim, 1 Go for the Throat). Two cards in one. First you cast Swift End as an instant: 3 mana, destroys any creature or planeswalker, and you lose 2 life. The card then goes to exile, and later you cast the 2/3 lifelink Rider from there. When the Rider dies it goes to the bottom of your library. Its 1BB cost suits the deck's black-heavy early turns better than the WW cards. It replaces the narrowest removal (Go for the Throat can't hit artifact creatures or planeswalkers) and two cards that each do only one job. The cheapest printing is a The List card (A$0.27 est), but the DRC and FIC printings are only about A$0.37 est, so any printing will do. *Also useful in: Mono-Black Midrange (60), Ghoulcaller Gisa Commander (Bracket 2, not a Game Changer).*
2. **1x Gideon, Ally of Zendikar** (replaces Seraph of the Sword). A 4-mana planeswalker. Its 0 ability makes a 2/2 Knight every turn, and its +1 turns it into a 5/5 indestructible attacker until end of turn. This deck kills most opposing creatures, so Gideon is hard to attack down. After Rider it's the biggest upgrade per dollar: one card of about A$2 at MTGMate (out of stock on 2026-09-28) for a large gain. The cheapest printing is The List (A$1.01 est), which AU shops may not stock. The original BFZ printing is only about A$2.12 est (US$1.49). *Also useful in: Giada Angels Commander (white; not a Game Changer).*
3. **3x Isolated Chapel** (replaces Scoured Barrens x2, Orzhov Guildgate). A W/B dual land that enters untapped if you control a Plains or Swamp. Mana is this deck's weak point. With 3 Chapel, 3 Snarl and 2 Caves, the chances on the play (counting missed land drops) change as follows: casting a turn-4 WW spell rises from about 49–54% to 61–62%, a turn-3 1BB spell from 65–69% to 70–72%, and a turn-4 WWW spell from 11–32% to 38–47%. In each range, the low figure assumes simple colour-balancing land play and the high figure assumes perfect sequencing. Most of the gain is on the white side. Reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. *Also useful in: Any W/B deck: 60-card Orzhov Vampires, a future Orzhov Commander deck.*
3. **3x Shineshadow Snarl** (replaces Temple of Silence, Swamp x2). A W/B dual land that enters untapped if you reveal a Plains or Swamp from your hand. It pairs with Chapel to replace the tapped duals (same simulation as above). It's the cheapest W/B dual that can enter untapped. Orzhov Basilica (A$0.33) always enters tapped, and Concealed Courtyard (A$1.52) and Shattered Sanctum (A$1.99) cost more. *Also useful in: Any W/B deck: 60-card Orzhov Vampires, a future Orzhov Commander deck.*
4. **2x Infernal Grasp** (replaces Stasis Snare x2). A 2-mana instant that destroys any creature, including artifact creatures, which Go for the Throat can't hit. You lose 2 life. It's cheaper than Stasis Snare, needs no WW, and enchantment removal can't undo it. *Also useful in: Mono-Black Midrange (60), Ghoulcaller Gisa Commander, Dimir Control.*
5. **1x Sorin the Mirthless** (replaces Phyrexian Arena). A 4-mana planeswalker. Each turn, its +1 lets you take the top card of your library into your hand (you lose life equal to that card's mana value, so a land costs nothing). Its -2 instead makes a 2/3 flying lifelink Vampire. That's card advantage that also affects the board, and the Vampires' lifelink wins back the life the +1 costs. Arena, by contrast, only ever drains 1 life a turn. *Also useful in: Ghoulcaller Gisa Commander, Mono-Black Midrange (60).*
6. **1x Elspeth, Sun's Champion** (replaces Massacre Wurm). A 6-mana bomb (a card that wins the game on its own if unanswered). Its +1 makes three 1/1 soldiers every turn, and its -3 destroys every creature with power 4 or more, including your own Lyra, Demon and Titan. It beats both wide boards and big creatures. It's cheap (A$2.53 est). Reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. *Also useful in: Giada Angels Commander (white; not a Game Changer).*
7. **2x Caves of Koilos** (replaces Swamp, Plains). A dual land that always enters untapped and deals 1 damage to you when tapped for W or B. It's the last and smallest piece of the mana fix. Playing a basic Swamp and Plains in these two slots (the owned list) costs about 1–3 points on the turn-3/turn-4 BB and WW colour checks, and 4–8 points on a turn-4 WWW spell such as Archangel of Tithes, depending on how well you sequence your lands. Buy these last. Reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. *Also useful in: Any W/B deck: 60-card Orzhov Vampires, a future Orzhov Commander deck.*

After the land upgrade it's closer to 1 in 2. Josu (2BB) is castable. Swap Archangel back in once the new lands arrive. |

On the owned mana, lands 1–3 often enter tapped. Play a tapped dual on turn 1 unless you're holding Swords to Plowshares for a turn-1 threat.

## Notes

### Game plan (in plain words)
- **Early (turns 1–3): answer, don't race.** Use cheap **removal** (spells that kill or exile a creature): Swords to Plowshares, Go for the Throat, Infernal Grasp, Fateful Absence and Hero's Downfall. Kill whatever the opponent plays. Knight of Grace, Knight of Malice, Vampire Nighthawk and Inspiring Overseer hold the ground and draw cards.
- **Middle (turns 4–5): land something they must answer.** Desecration Demon, Kalitas, Court of Grace, Gideon, Sorin or Lyra. Keep killing their creatures so your threats stay safe.
- **Late: take over.** Grave Titan, Elspeth, the Court's Angels and Lyra's lifelink flyers win the long game. Castle Locthwain (a land) draws extra cards when you have spare mana.
- You win when the opponent runs out of threats before you run out of removal. A card that does two jobs is a **2-for-1**: you spend one card and they lose two. Examples are Murderous Rider (kills something, then becomes a creature), Overseer (a flyer that draws a card) and planeswalkers that make a creature every turn.

### Jargon used below
- **Instant**: a spell you can cast during the opponent's turn.
- **Flash**: lets a creature or enchantment be cast like an instant.
- **Planeswalker**: a permanent with loyalty counters. You use one of its abilities each turn, and the opponent can attack it to remove loyalty.
- **Monarch** (Court of Grace): you draw an extra card at the end of each of your turns. If a creature deals combat damage to you, its controller becomes monarch instead.
- **Legend rule**: if you control two legendary permanents with the same name, you keep one and the other goes to the graveyard. So hold the second Lyra in your hand until the first one dies.
- **Adventure** (Murderous Rider): you can cast the instant half (Swift End) first. The card then goes to exile, and later you can cast the creature half from there. You can also just cast the Rider as a creature. When the Rider dies it goes to the bottom of your library, not the graveyard.

### Opening hand and mulligans
- **Keep:** 2–4 lands with at least one cheap removal spell or 2–3-drop. The best hands have both colours (a Swamp plus a Plains or dual) and one or two 1–2-mana removal spells.
- **Also keep:** 5 lands plus strong spells (Night's Whisper, Overseer, a bomb). This deck is happy to hit land drops.
- **Mulligan** (shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken): hands with 0–1 lands or 6–7 lands, and 2-land hands made only of 4- to 6-drops when you're on the play.
- **Colour check:** 2 Plains with only black spells (or the reverse) is risky. Keep it only if it has 3+ lands or card draw.
- About 86% of 7-card hands have 2–5 lands. About 65% have a 1–2-mana removal spell (about 60% with the owned list).

### Play tips
1. **Save the best removal for the best threats.** Use Go for the Throat or Infernal Grasp on early creatures; Go for the Throat can't hit artifact creatures. Save three answers for the scary cards: Swords to Plowshares (exile beats 'indestructible'), and Hero's Downfall and Swift End (they also kill planeswalkers). Save Stroke of Midnight for what only it can answer: artifacts, enchantments and planeswalkers. It leaves the opponent a 1/1.
2. **Leave mana up on their turn.** Nearly all the removal is instant. Kill an attacker during combat, or at the end of their turn so you still use all your mana.
3. **Clear the board before playing a planeswalker,** then protect it. Use Gideon's 0 (make a 2/2 Knight) and Sorin's -2 (make a 2/3 flying lifelinker) to make blockers. While Archangel of Tithes is untapped, attacking you or your planeswalkers costs the opponent {1} per creature.
4. **Watch your life total.** Night's Whisper, Infernal Grasp, Swift End, Caves of Koilos, Castle Locthwain and Sorin's +1 all cost life. Against fast red decks, count before you pay.
5. **Play lands in the right order.** Play a basic Swamp or Plains early so Isolated Chapel comes in untapped later. Keep a basic in hand to reveal for Shineshadow Snarl.
6. **Know your own cards' catches.** Elspeth's -3 also kills *your* Lyra, Demon and Titan (power 4 or more). At the start of each combat, the opponent may sacrifice a creature to tap Desecration Demon, which then gets a +1/+1 counter. While Kalitas is out, any nontoken creature of theirs that would die is exiled instead, and you get a 2/2 Zombie.

### Watch out for (from the opponent)
- **Board wipes** (Wrath of God, Damnation and similar): don't put every creature out at once. Planeswalkers and Court of Grace survive a creature wipe.
- **Hexproof or protection creatures** can't be targeted. In the target list, use Elspeth's -3 (power 4+), blockers, or Massacre Wurm or Fumigate from the sideboard. The owned-list sideboard also has the edicts Tribute to Hunger and Consumed by Greed, which make the opponent sacrifice a creature.
- **Indestructible creatures** ignore 'destroy'. Use Swords to Plowshares or Stasis Snare (they exile) or Massacre Wurm's -2/-2.
- **Counterspells** (blue): cast a less important spell first to draw the counter out. Bring in Duress from the sideboard.
- **Enchantments and artifacts** (Pacifism on Lyra, equipment, mana rocks): in the main deck, Stroke of Midnight answers any of them. Mortify answers enchantments but not artifacts. The sideboard has Disenchant, Generous Gift and Cathar Commando.
- **Graveyard decks** (reanimation, recursion): Soul-Guide Lantern in the sideboard.

### Sideboard guide (target list)
The sideboard is optional and is for best-of-three against stronger opponents. Swap cards one-for-one so the deck stays at 60.
- **Against lots of small creatures or tokens:** bring in Massacre Wurm, Fumigate and Sunblast Angel. Take out Night's Whisper ×3, whose life cost hurts against fast decks. Keep the first-strike Knights, which block small creatures well.
- **Against control or counterspells (few creatures):** bring in Duress ×2, Phyrexian Arena, Seraph of the Sword and Linvala. Take out Go for the Throat ×2, Infernal Grasp ×2 and 1 Swords to Plowshares. Keep Fateful Absence, Downfall and Swift End for their planeswalkers.
- **Against artifacts or enchantments:** bring in Generous Gift, Disenchant and Cathar Commando. Take out Go for the Throat ×2 and Knight of Malice.
- **Against graveyard decks:** bring in Soul-Guide Lantern and take out 1 Night's Whisper.
- **Against removal-heavy decks:** bring in Valorous Stance (it can make Lyra or Demon indestructible) and Linvala. Take out a Go for the Throat and a Knight.
- **Owned-list sideboard:** the same ideas.
  - Against control: Duress ×3.
  - Against go-wide decks: Fumigate, Sunblast Angel or Archangel.
  - Against artifacts: Disenchant or Cathar Commando.
  - Against hexproof creatures: Tribute to Hunger or Consumed by Greed.
  - Against green or white creatures: Deathmark.
